Rules for anyone, person or agent, changing shell code here. A rule marked **enforced** is decided by `tests/test_slop.zsh` or `tests/test_setup.zsh`, which run in `tests/run.sh` and in CI: breaking it fails the build with the rule's name in the message. The rest need judgment and are checked in review.

The idea is borrowed from lint-rule sets that reject low-signal patterns: a rule a machine can decide belongs in a test, not in prose that has to be remembered.

## Before you write

> tl;dr: the smallest change that works, proven by a test that fails without it.

- Look for the existing helper first: `setup/lib/` for setup, `tests/lib.zsh` for tests, `zshrc/config/helpers/` for the shell.
- No new abstraction, flag or file for a case that does not exist yet. Three similar lines are better than a helper with one caller.
- Every behaviour change ships with a test case in `tests/test_<area>.zsh` that fails without it. Run `tests/run.sh` before finishing.
- Never present a guess as fact. A shape you have not seen (a command's flags, a file's format) is checked against the real thing before code depends on it.

## Enforced rules

> tl;dr: eight pattern rules plus the component contract, the no-empty-section rule (a failure under `SETUP_STRICT_REPORT=1`) and two linters; the failing test prints the rule name.

| Rule | What is rejected | Do this instead | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `remote-installer` | `curl ... \| sh` and `sh -c "$(curl ...)"` | `run_remote_installer URL INTERPRETER` in `setup/lib/download.sh`, which downloads in full with retries before running | every shell file |
| `disable-needs-reason` | `# shellcheck disable=SC1234` with nothing after it | add the reason on the same line, or fix the warning | every shell file |
| `packages-are-data` | `brew install` or `brew tap` in setup code | add a line to `Brewfile` | `setup.sh`, `setup/` except `bootstrap-darwin.sh`, which installs bash before the Brewfile can be read |
| `no-swallowed-errors` | `\|\| true` and `\|\| :` | handle it: `\|\| say_warn "what failed and what happens now"`, or `\|\| return 1` | `setup.sh`, `setup/` |
| `no-exit-in-components` | `exit` in `setup/lib` or `setup/components` | `return`; the runner decides whether the run stops | `setup/` |
| `platform-seam: probe` | `$OSTYPE`, `uname`, `sw_vers` outside `setup/lib/platform.sh` | declare the platform in `define_component` | `setup.sh`, `setup/` |
| `platform-seam: macOS-only command` | `launchctl`, `osascript`, `pbcopy`, `brew`, `chsh`, `defaults read/write`, a `/Library/` path in a component not declared `darwin` | move it to a `darwin` component or a `*-darwin.sh` lib file | `setup/` except `darwin` components and `*-darwin.sh` |
| `stage-zero-is-bash-3.2` | bash 4+ syntax (`declare -A`, `local -n`, `mapfile`, `wait -n`, `${var,,}`, `${var@Q}`, `\|&`, `coproc`) in a stage 0 file | keep stage 0 to finding or installing bash 5; put the logic in a file loaded after the restart | `setup.sh`, `setup/lib/{ui,platform,download,bootstrap-*}.sh` |
| no empty section | a `== name` header with nothing printed under it, in any phase, whatever the step returns | every component says what this run did, by name (`say_ok "Convert to WebP"`, `say_ok "130 font files copied into …"`); the runner's closing line for a silent step is a safety net, not the report: with `SETUP_STRICT_REPORT=1`, which the tests and CI set, a silent step fails the run | `setup/lib/runner.sh` |
| component contract | a component file missing from `COMPONENT_ORDER` (or the reverse), no install or check step, an unknown platform or requirement | see "Adding a setup component" | `setup/components/` |
| `lint` | shellcheck findings at style level, shfmt differences | fix them; `shfmt -w -i 4 -ci -sr setup.sh setup` | `setup.sh`, `setup/` |

Each pattern rule carries a sample that must trip it, so a pattern edited into uselessness fails too. To add a rule, add a `forbid` call with its sample in `tests/test_slop.zsh` and a row here.

## Adding a setup component

> tl;dr: one file with install and check, one line in COMPONENT_ORDER; a plain package is a Brewfile line, not a component.

1. Create `setup/components/<name>.sh`:

   ```bash
   # shellcheck shell=bash
   define_component zoxide all optional "zoxide directory jumper"

   component_zoxide_install() {    # must be safe to run again
       ...
   }

   component_zoxide_check() {      # read-only; one `check` line per fact
       check --warn --hint "run: setup.sh init --only zoxide" "zoxide is on PATH" command -v zoxide
   }
   ```

2. Add the name to `COMPONENT_ORDER` in `setup/lib/registry.sh`, after whatever it needs.
3. `component_<name>_update` is optional; without it `setup.sh update` runs install again.
4. `required` only when later components cannot work without it. An optional component warns and returns 0 for a normal absence (no access to a private repo), returns 1 for a real failure.

## Judgment rules

> tl;dr: comments say why, names say what, output goes through the ui helpers, write for the latest bash and nothing but bash.

- Comments explain why, never what: the constraint, the ordering, the bug a line prevents. One sentence per line, no hard wrapping, no history, no commented-out code.
- A function name says what it returns or does (`shell_rc_is_linked`, `brew_bash_path`), so call sites read without a comment.
- Setup code prints through `say_ok`, `say_warn`, `say_fail`, `say_info`; a bare `echo` is for a function's return value.
- A question to the user goes through `confirm`, which answers no without a terminal and yes under `--yes`.
- Write for the latest bash. `setup.sh` restarts itself under Homebrew's bash 5 before loading anything else, so use associative arrays, `mapfile`, namerefs and `wait -n` where they make the code simpler. Only stage 0 is held to bash 3.2 (enforced above), because it is the code that installs bash 5.
- No other language for setup. When logic outgrows shell (real concurrency, data structures, a parser), it becomes a Go tool installed by a component, not a cleverer script.
- Secrets never appear in code, tests, fixtures or output. `zshrc/aliases/secrets/` is not read aloud or committed.
